Tagcast 0.70.0 adds CSV playlist import, complete metadata exports, playlist covers
and folders, separate artist credits and optional album and artist background texts.
The Electron desktop apps and Python/browser version share all these features.

## Import and organise playlists

- Import CSV/TSV files, map columns and match tracks against your loaded library.
  Track title and performing artist are required; album, album artist, duration,
  year and track number can improve matching.
- Unique exact matches are selected automatically. Unresolved records explain
  differences and offer suggestions and a library search for manual selection.
- Create a playlist from the selected matches without resolving every remaining
  row. The final review shows which records will be omitted.
- Export unresolved records with their original columns and order for later
  review or re-import. Download before closing the import dialog; drafts are not
  retained across restarts.
- Browse native playlist folders, create and rename folders, and review adding
  or removing playlist references. Change a playlist cover after comparing images.
- Open playlists above 10,000 tracks in pages of 100. Large-playlist playback uses
  the current page; full-content editing remains limited to 10,000 tracks.

## Complete library metadata export

- **Settings → Export library metadata** prepares JSON or a ZIP of linked CSVs.
  Exports include separate album artists, ordered credit roles and phrases, exact
  genres, native IDs, ratings and upload dates, plus available optional tags,
  playlists, folders and local favourites.
- Export uses the loaded library without extra iBroadcast requests or metadata
  writes. Reload first for a fresh snapshot. Audio, images, credentials and provider
  prose are excluded. This metadata archive has no restore function.
- Schema 2 correctly separates playlist-folder references from music track IDs,
  preserving playlist order and repeated positions.

## Artists, credits and favourites

- Edit additional album artists and full track credits, including composer,
  lyricist, conductor and other native roles, with optional credit phrases.
  Existing IDs, order and unfamiliar roles are preserved until explicitly changed.
- Choose existing artists, genres and composers from local searchable suggestions,
  or type a new name. Choosing a suggestion changes only the draft.
- **Cleanup → Album artists** previews semicolon-separated names, keeps the first
  primary and saves the rest as separate additional artists after approval.
  Existing separate credits are preserved; writes use checked, bounded batches.
- One **Favourites** page has Tracks, Albums and Album artists tabs. Album and
  artist hearts are local per account, independently of native iBroadcast stars.
- Rate album artists with native stars. Sort artists and albums by rating, and
  albums by upload date. Track thumbs-down uses native rating 1; the heart uses 5.
  A dislike does not skip a track or remove music.

## Background texts and browsing

- Optional TheAudioDB artist biographies and album information are off by default.
  They load only for visited artists/albums and are cached locally. No Premium key
  is bundled or required for these lookups.
- Available bundled 1001 Albums texts take priority over TheAudioDB, including
  when the discovery page is disabled or no analysis has been run. Attribution
  and license links stay visible. The reference catalogue also has reviewed
  title, credit and release-year corrections.
- Album artists and Albums each have one Filter and sort menu. Empty filters are
  omitted while the current choice and All remain reachable.
- A visible message and moving progress bar show library loading and reloading.
  The bar has no percentage because the request does not provide reliable progress.
- The Sound button has a speaker-cabinet icon, player colours follow the palette
  where supported, and track rows, breadcrumbs and back-button spacing are refined.
- **Export changes** is now in **Settings → Change history**. Electron's Help
  menu opens the GitHub Wiki.

## Reliability

- Concurrent API requests, streaming and artwork uploads share token refresh;
  delayed failures and credential saves cannot overwrite a newer connection.
- Genre validation consistently accepts up to 200 Unicode characters per label
  and 20 labels per track. Oversized input is reported and retained for editing,
  rather than silently shortened.
- Artist-profile, rating and stale-response fixes preserve drafts, current
  playback and account boundaries. Accepted writes continue to be read back.

## Downloads and upgrading

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.70.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.70.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.70.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.70.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Every archive has a SHA-256 companion. Keep the complete extracted package together.
**Quit the older Tagcast before starting 0.70.0.** Settings, sign-in and local
account favourites stay in the existing Tagcast settings folder. Browser-local
preferences and Change history remain separate from Electron's profile.

macOS apps have an ad-hoc integrity signature, without Developer ID notarization;
Windows downloads are not Authenticode signed. See the
[installation guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/Getting-started)
and [full user guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki).
Tagcast never changes your local music files and does not install updates automatically.
